correctness.rationale: For independent component lifetimes with G(x)=exp[-alpha(-log x)^beta] on (0,1) and N>=1 geometric with weights (1-rho)rho^{n-1}, summing E[(1-G)^N] yields S_Y=(1-rho)(1-G)/(1-rho+rho G). Differentiation gives f_Y=(1-rho)g/(1-rho+rho G)^2 and h=g/[(1-G)(1-rho+rho G)]. Writing t=-log x, at right t downarrow0, 1-G~alpha t^beta, g~alpha beta t^{beta-1}/x and the geometric denominator tends to 1. Thus (1-x)h->beta, strictly positive for every alpha,beta>0 and 0<rho<1. Right-endpoint divergence contradicts a globally nonincreasing or ultimately nonincreasing hazard. For x downarrow0, h~alpha beta t^{beta-1}exp(t-alpha t^beta)/(1-rho), giving exactly the stated five left limits; for beta<1 both endpoint divergences force an interior minimum by continuity. Independently verified five high-precision right-endpoint triples and five left-endpoint cases; these finite checks do not prove the infinite claim.

originality.rationale: Best-of-knowledge originality concerns the identified false global hazard-shape claims for the specific 2026 unit-Weibull geometric minimum model, accompanied by its explicit sharp terminal coefficient and left-endpoint classification. The 2026 source explicitly advertises decreasing and unimodal hazard regimes, while its own Figure 2 curves rise near one. The 2008 Weibull-geometric precursor is an unbounded-support construction and permits decreasing hazards there; the 2019 unit-Weibull source provides the baseline but not this compound-model correction. The generic finite-support cumulative-hazard identity already rules out any ultimately bounded hazard, so the method and qualitative obstruction are elementary, not a new general theorem. Searches located no prior independent correction with the model-specific endpoint computation. Novelty is narrow and qualified by the inaccessible full 2026 paper.

value.rationale: The 2026 paper prominently markets decreasing and unimodal hazard shapes for its bounded lifetime family. Demonstrating their impossibility on the complete support, with an exact right-endpoint coefficient and the five-case left-endpoint behavior, is a motivated correction of a specific published reliability-model claim and a useful warning against truncated-plot shape inference. Its value is as a focused diagnostic counterexample/boundary result, not as a new general theorem. The underlying finite-endpoint hazard fact is textbook-level and the calculation elementary; the concrete published model error and sharp coefficient supply the substantive reason this limited finding matters.
residual_risks: Practical impact is restricted to shape-class terminology and model selection; no full classification of critical points or inferential improvement is shown.
If the 2026 paper uses only finite-window descriptive terminology, the correction applies specifically to standard global categories.

limitations: Original article full body inaccessible despite arXiv/OA search and lawful institutional attempt (vpn_disconnected); no claim of whole-document noncoverage.
No general hazard theorem is asserted; no full critical-point census.
The five-case left endpoint is analytic; finite checks are only corroboration.
Publication withheld due to public operational metadata privacy, not because scientific C/O/V failed.
